world-lifecycle/v2.mutationCaller: desktop-bridge, shell-ui through lifecycle dispatch only

WorldConnectionInventoryChanged.trigger: Emit only after an actual change in the authorized installed Adapter connection inventory/capability revision. receipt.result is the new authorized inventory snapshot. ListWorldConnections by itself does not change state or require this event.
WorldConnectionInventoryChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

WorldConnectionSelectionChanged.trigger: Emit only after successful durable selection of a changed connection/world; receipt.result is the resulting current context. Failed/no-change selection emits nothing.
WorldConnectionSelectionChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

ActiveWorldChanged.trigger: Emit only after successful durable switch to a different world; receipt.result is the resulting current context. Preserve currentSession and clear out-of-world selection.
ActiveWorldChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

ObjectInventoryChanged.trigger: Emit only on an actual durable object registry revision/inventory change; receipt.result is the new authorized object inventory snapshot. A ListObjects read by itself need not emit.
ObjectInventoryChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

ObjectCreated.trigger: Emit only after verified creating transaction and durable registration of the stable object; receipt.result is the newly registered object. No event for pending/failed readback.
ObjectCreated.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

ObjectNameChanged.trigger: Emit only after successful atomic name/registry CAS that actually changes the display name/key; operation NameObject or RenameObject selects the exact receipt variant. receipt.result is the new name/registry state; failure/no-change emits nothing.
ObjectNameChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

ActiveObjectSelectionReplaced.trigger: Emit only after a successful complete ordered selection replacement with a new selectionRevision. receipt.result is the resulting selection, including empty-array clear; failure leaves old selection and emits nothing.
ActiveObjectSelectionReplaced.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

ObjectInspectionInvalidated.trigger: Emit only when a previously valid INSPECTED snapshot is invalidated by an observed different world revision. receipt contains the prior successful ObjectInspection with the now-invalid snapshot; it is neither new facts nor a new successful inspect. newWorldRevision is the actually observed revision, unequal to receipt.result.worldRevision. An InspectObject query alone need not emit; consumer must discard prior facts for later painter/apply.
ObjectInspectionInvalidated.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

AffectedObjectAnalysisReady.trigger: Emit after successful complete analysis at bound revisions; receipt.result is that immutable analysis. No event for incomplete/stale/failed analysis.
AffectedObjectAnalysisReady.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

AffectedObjectNotificationRequired.trigger: Emit only for successful policy decision BLOCK_AND_NOTIFY on nonselected affected objects; receipt.result carries the displayed immutable affected set/decision revision. NO_NOTIFICATION/CONTINUE/CANCEL do not emit this signal.
AffectedObjectNotificationRequired.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

TransactionAppliedPendingReadback.trigger: Emit only after actual apply has reached APPLIED_PENDING_READBACK; receipt.result is the matching pending transaction receipt. This signal is not verified world/product success and never advances history.
TransactionAppliedPendingReadback.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

TransactionVerified.trigger: Emit only after full matched readback and durable linked history, status VERIFIED. receipt.result is the final verified transaction receipt; pending/restore failure/history persist failure never emits.
TransactionVerified.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

HistoryPositionChanged.trigger: Emit only after the whole linked Undo or Redo transaction is VERIFIED with durable movement of all linked heads; operation Undo/Redo is the finite signal discriminator/direction. receipt.result is that verified receipt. Conflict proposal, rollback/failure and unchanged heads emit nothing.
HistoryPositionChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

HistoryInventoryChanged.trigger: Emit only after an actual durable linked history inventory/head change; receipt.result is the new safe history snapshot. HistoryQuery read alone need not emit.
HistoryInventoryChanged.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; actual runtime event emission NOT_RUN

placementSettings.name: placement.frontGapCells
placementSettings.meaning: Cells between the anchor player's feet cell and the near edge of the new building, along the player's facing direction.
placementSettings.consequence: Larger values start the building further away; 0 starts it in the cell directly in front of the feet cell. The player's own body is still excluded by the body-occupancy rule.
placementSettings.whenUnsetOrInvalid: InspectPlacementRegion returns CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE / validate / POLICY_UNAVAILABLE with unavailableSettings naming this setting; nothing is inspected or written; no hidden default is used.

placementSettings.name: placement.forwardSearchCells
placementSettings.meaning: How many further cells forward the building may be shifted when the nearest position is not usable.
placementSettings.consequence: 0 means no forward search: the first position is used or the user is asked. Larger values search further before asking.
placementSettings.whenUnsetOrInvalid: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE / POLICY_UNAVAILABLE naming this setting; zero inspection and zero writes.

placementSettings.name: placement.lateralSearchCells
placementSettings.meaning: Maximum sideways shift on each side, perpendicular to the facing direction.
placementSettings.whenUnsetOrInvalid: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE / POLICY_UNAVAILABLE naming this setting; zero inspection and zero writes.

placementSettings.name: placement.verticalSearchCells
placementSettings.meaning: Maximum up or down shift of the building's ground level from the player's feet level.
placementSettings.consequence: 0 means the building must stand at the player's feet level.
placementSettings.whenUnsetOrInvalid: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE / POLICY_UNAVAILABLE naming this setting; zero inspection and zero writes.

placementInvariants.text: World and transport incarnation must match the current selection.
placementInvariants.consequence: A changed connection or world rejects stale work.

placementInvariants.text: Only Canvas decides transactions; Adapter only transports; Painter and Brush do not write.
placementInvariants.consequence: Model output goes through Painter and Brush before Canvas.

placementInvariants.text: Success requires complete actual readback and durable same-transaction history.
placementInvariants.consequence: Pending or unknown does not become success.

placementInvariants.text: Failure restores the complete saved before image and verifies it by readback.
placementInvariants.consequence: Undo retains the original transaction and its saved state.

placementInvariants.text: Existing object footprints and inspection records are checked before mutation.
placementInvariants.consequence: Unresolved object conflicts reject the fresh-build entry.

placementInvariants.owner: Painter and Brush (supplied facts); Adapter engine (actual bodies)
placementInvariants.text: Coverage, static materials, geometry and hazards remain checked against supplied facts; actual player bodies are checked inside the engine at inspection and before every write.
placementInvariants.consequence: Invalid geometry or occupied body cells reject before writes.

placementInvariants.text: A placement shown to the player as a structured PlacementProposal and confirmed by a new human message is part of the confirmed intent; the submitted world effect set must match it (EXACT_CELLS: the same cells; ANCHORED_EXTENT: inside the confirmed bounds on the same inspection).
placementInvariants.consequence: A changed view, World, frame, inspection or target is refused by name and needs a new proposal and a new human confirmation; it is never re-based silently. A build confirmed without a structured placement keeps the normal CURRENT_VIEW placement.

settingsSurface.rule: Show each setting name, owner, current value, default, scope and consequence. Show invariants read-only.

protocolPolicy.rule: Runtime compatibility is decided per protocol by exact major equality, advertised minor >= required minor, and presence of every required capability. Package version, patch, source revision and artifact digest are provenance only and never decide compatibility.
protocolPolicy.majors: Protocol majors are explicit integers >= 1 declared here; they are independent of the 0.x npm package version. A package version alone (0.x or otherwise) never implies compatibility, and a peer that advertises no ProtocolHandshake is not compatible.
protocolPolicy.minor: Within one major a minor may only add new operations, new types or new capability ids, or a qualified optional field. Adding a required field or an enum value to an existing type of that major, or changing a meaning, requires a new major. A qualified optional field (since 1.1.0) is additive only when all hold: (1) it is not in `required` and has no null form, and its absence keeps exactly the previous meaning, so every previous-minor value stays valid with unchanged digests; (2) no existing field, enum, constant, wire identifier or capability id changes; (3) a previous-minor strict decoder (additionalProperties:false) refuses a value that carries it (UNKNOWN_REQUIRED_FIELD), so the new capability fails closed and is never silently ignored. tools/compare-major.mjs checks (1) and (2) structurally; (3) is a property of the strict decoder and is shown by the cross-version gate.
protocolPolicy.rejection: Missing protocol, different major or lower minor: UNSUPPORTED_VERSION/decode/VERSION_UNSUPPORTED. Missing capability: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/decode/VERSION_UNSUPPORTED. Both are decided before any world write.
protocolPolicy.legacy: checkContractHandshake (and checkBuildProposalHandshake) decide the package by the same rule as checkContractsVersion: same package name, well-formed semver, equal major; minor, patch and prerelease are provenance. Required wires, compiledOperationsVersion and fact profiles are still checked separately, so a version match never implies an interface. There is no migration of old wires or profiles.
protocolPolicy.digestDomain: Region projections use the protocol domain 'HanaWorlds|region-voxels/v2|' so a different package patch yields the same digest.
protocolPolicy.schema: checkSchemaCompatibility applies the same major predicate to a peer schema bundle ($id) or profile (version); every type the caller relies on must still be present (CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/decode/VERSION_UNSUPPORTED).
protocolPolicy.minorWires: A wire added in a minor (minorWires, with the version that added it) is advertised in contractHandshake.wireVersions but is not required by the default checkContractHandshake: a peer of an earlier minor of the same major stays compatible, and a caller that relies on the added wire requires it explicitly. Operations appended to an existing wire raise that protocol minor (protocolMinors); the existing operations of the wire keep their order and shapes.

regionCapabilities.meaning: Pure compile of RegionBuildProjection into chunks cut along the partition the request carries (the world source's declared partition); unspecified cells stay unspecified, the empty material stays an explicit carve.
Existing per-cell BUILD/V5 compilation to operations/v4 is retained.
Validates coordinates, extent, palette legality and empty-material carve of a skill region proposal on the existing proposal channel; never writes the world or plans on its own.
Reads RegionState per chunk in bulk.
Loads unloaded chunks and reads them back before reporting KNOWN; anything still unknown is reported UNKNOWN with the world source's opaque reason code.
Writes per chunk after comparing expectedCurrentDigest; returns per-chunk facts and never claims an atomic transaction.
Writes a complete RegionState (material, orientation, empty material and per-cell state) for rollback or Undo.

A world source that declares postWriteLighting REQUIRED returns a COMPLETE lighting fact only after the light recalculation for the written box has finished; one that declares NONE returns no lighting fact.
One logical transaction across all chunks; success only after the full region readback summary equals the expected summary.
Any failed, unknown or mismatching chunk restores the whole pre-write region.
Durably stores the complete pre-write RegionSnapshotContent with a mature compressor and records RegionSnapshotRef.
Undo restores the whole region of the same transaction after checking current world, history and current summary.
Per-cell writes and restores use the CALLBACK_FREE_WRITE path of write-path-init/v1.
Region writes and restores use the CALLBACK_FREE_WRITE path of write-path-init/v1.
Catalogue placeable is published under scope write-path-init/v1 and agrees with a WritePathEvidence inventory (validateCatalogueWritePathFacts).

Every ROLLED_BACK RegionCommitResult carries rollbackCause: the failure Canvas itself observed in this transaction that made it restore (an Adapter error and guard refusal relayed unchanged, or Canvas's own readback/lighting/transport finding), bound to the same transactionId; it is stored with the terminal outcome and returned unchanged on exact replay.
Undo only cells specified by committed origin operations, verified from bound before/after snapshots; preserve actual outside state through source CAS. No region Redo.

regionInvariants.text: A null run is UNSPECIFIED: the cell is not written and keeps its current state. Only an explicit palette entry of the Catalogue emptyMaterialRef carves.
regionInvariants.consequence: Unspecified cells are never turned into the empty material.

regionInvariants.text: Unloaded chunks are loaded and read back first; a chunk that is still UNKNOWN rejects the write.
regionInvariants.consequence: Unknown terrain is never overwritten blindly.

regionInvariants.text: All chunks of one region form one Canvas transaction; partial chunk success is never a commit and triggers whole rollback.
regionInvariants.consequence: No partial region remains after a failure.

regionInvariants.text: Undo restores the complete pre-write snapshot of the same transaction only when the current summary still equals that transaction's verified after summary.
regionInvariants.consequence: External edits are not silently overwritten.

regionInvariants.text: Peers are compatible when protocol majors match and required capabilities are present; package hashes are provenance only.
regionInvariants.consequence: Different patch builds interoperate; a different major or missing capability is rejected before writing.

regionInvariants.text: placeable is a fact about the declared callback-free write and initialization path only; unknown or side-effecting initialization rejects the write, and UNKNOWN is never treated as true.
regionInvariants.consequence: Plain materials such as stone can be written; materials that need initialization or carry state are refused before writing; later independent changes surface as readback/Undo conflicts.

regionInvariants.text: A region rollback cause states only the failure the transaction owner observed inside the transaction's own operation boxes, using the closed ErrorCode/ErrorReason/GuardRefusal values. It never names who or what else changed the world (natural simulation, other writers, test instrumentation) and never covers cells outside the operation boxes. An absent cause is UNKNOWN, never a guessed cause.
regionInvariants.consequence: A rolled-back region tells the player and the skill why Canvas restored, without inventing an engine cause; a missing cause is shown as unknown.

writePathStateScope.writePathMeaning: The declared write and restore path sets material and orientation as bulk data. The engine runs no material-definition callback and creates no per-cell state on this path; fields the StateProfile declares derived are recomputed by the engine. A world source declares that its per-cell and region writes use exactly this path with the capabilities world-adapter/v8:callback-free-write and world-adapter-region/v3:callback-free-write.

factsMeaning.placeable: true only when the definition defines none of initializationCallbacks or stateIndicatorCallbacks and globalWriteCallbacks is known to be empty, i.e. writing (and later restoring) this material on this path runs no skipped lifecycle callback and can leave no per-cell state. false when an initialization callback is defined. null when the definition callback inventory or the global write-path callback inventory is unknown or non-empty, or when only state indicators are defined. Never inferred from opaque engine code; UNKNOWN is never defaulted to true.

writePathStateScope.globalWriteCallbacks: Names of engine global callback registries that fire on this path and currently have handlers. Must be an empty set for any true placeable fact; null or non-empty forces null for every material.
outOfScope: Player-triggered node callbacks (on_punch, on_dig, after_dig_node, on_rightclick, can_dig, on_rotate and global punch/dig handlers)
Independent world dynamics (ABM, LBM, on_blast, on_flood, other mods' later actions)
Mod-private custom fields that the engine never calls on this path
External effects that a replaced node's skipped on_destruct/after_destruct would have had outside its own cell
writePathStateScope.guards: Out-of-scope later changes are not claimed absent. They are detected by the complete RegionState readback (material, orientation and per-cell state) and its summary digest, and by same-transaction Undo rejecting with UNDO_CONFLICT/EXTERNAL_EDIT_CONFLICT when the current summary no longer equals the verified after summary. Canvas still decides every transaction.

sessionWorldSeam.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; Canvas/Workshop/Adapter provider implementations and real runtime NOT_RUN

authority.sessionToWorldSelection: Canvas only (canvas/v7 ReadWorldSelectionContext/SelectWorldConnection/SwitchWorldConnection, plus the added canvas/v7 UnselectWorldConnection, RetireSessionSelection, ListWorldSelections, ReserveWorldRetirement, ReleaseWorldRetirement). selectionRevision is generated only by Canvas.
authority.sessionIdentityAndLifecycle: Workshop (session/v5, including the added ReadSessionIdentity/ListSessions). Authenticity comes from the Host-bound internal port, never from request JSON; a syntax-valid Ref is not evidence that a Session exists. sessionRevision in SessionIdentity is the same Workshop revision carried as CurrentContext.sessionRevision / UNBOUND.sessionRevision.
authority.nativeReadinessAndTransport: Adapter (world-adapter/v8 DiscoverConnections/ListWorlds/ReadLocalConnection, LocalEngineControlPort). Adapter keeps no Session-to-World table and never generates selectionRevision.
authority.worldDeletion: Adapter-local world management, serialized through the Canvas retirement reservation below. No new shared-world write authority.

sequences.selectSession: Before SelectWorldConnection/SwitchWorldConnection, Canvas reads the Session through session/v5 ReadSessionIdentity on its Host-bound port; SESSION_NOT_FOUND rejects. A known Session without a world reads UNBOUND from ReadWorldSelectionContext.
sequences.unbind: UnselectWorldConnection(expectedRevision, expectedContext) compares with the Canvas current selection; success returns CurrentContext with activeWorldRef null, localContext null and no selected objects. The Session then reads UNBOUND and disappears from ListWorldSelections for that world.
sequences.deleteSession: Precondition: the Workshop provider actually supports persistent deletion (existing SessionSnapshot.sessionDeleteSupported / PublicCapabilities.sessionDeleteSupported is true). If it is false, DeleteSession fails with the existing SESSION_DELETE_UNSUPPORTED (reason DELETE_SEAM_ABSENT), RetireSessionSelection is NOT called, and the Session and its Canvas selection stay unchanged. If it is true, Workshop calls RetireSessionSelection first; Canvas atomically clears any selection and refuses further selection/read for that sessionRef with SESSION_NOT_FOUND. Workshop then performs the persistent deletion and returns DeleteSessionReceipt; deleted:true is reported only after the provider's own readback shows the Session gone. Releasing or disposing live handles (agent, store, scope) is not deletion and never yields deleted:true. Retirement is irreversible: if the persistent deletion then fails, the Session stays retired (not selectable) and DeleteSession returns its failure; it is never silently restored or reported deleted.
sequences.deleteWorld: Adapter reads ListWorldSelections, applies requireWorldRetirable, then ReserveWorldRetirement(expectedInventoryRevision). While a reservation exists Canvas rejects SelectWorldConnection/SwitchWorldConnection to that world with TRANSACTION_CONFLICT/SCOPE_DENIED. Adapter deletes its world, then ReleaseWorldRetirement(RETIRED); after RETIRED Canvas rejects selection of that worldRef with WORLD_NOT_FOUND. On an Adapter deletion failure it releases with ABORTED and the world stays selectable.

namedFailures.case: stale selection or inventory revision / context
unselect a world that is not the Session's current world
retire a world still selected by any Session, or select a world under retirement reservation
stale connection incarnation on a world-bound request
Workshop provider without persistent Session deletion

clarifications.C1: ReadWorldSelectionContext.worldRef names the world whose connection inventory is returned; it never selects. selection reports the Session's own selection: UNBOUND means the Session has no current World; when BOUND, selection.context.activeWorldRef is the Session's current World and may differ from request.worldRef.
clarifications.C2: A BOUND selection keeps the last actual LocalWorldContext Canvas selected (CurrentContext requires activeWorldRef === localContext.worldRef, so BOUND with localContext null is not valid). Whether it is connected now is derived by comparing that context with Adapter's current ConnectionInventory: the same connectionRef, worldRef and connectionIncarnationRef with readiness READY is CONNECTED; otherwise SELECTED_NOT_CONNECTED, which must not be shown as trusted-current and is rejected for writes by the existing CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH check. describeSelectionConnection implements this pure comparison.
clarifications.C3: When the owning runtime observes its native process exit, Adapter removes that connection from ConnectionInventory and changes capabilityRevision; a reopened world gets a new connectionIncarnationRef. No Readiness value is added and NativeControlEvidence gains no exit field.

sessionWorldSeam.selectedObjectSnapshot: Existing typed route: ReadWorldSelectionContext (BOUND context.orderedSelectedObjectRefs, selectionRevision, localContext) and canvas/v7 ListObjects (ObjectInventory.registryRevision, ObjectRecord.objectRevision) under the same localContext. A single atomic selected-object/objectRevision snapshot with zero/multiple selection rules is not added in this seam; it remains an open supply item.
sessionWorldSeam.compatibility: Additive only, as protocol minors within the existing majors (protocolPolicy): session/v5 minor 1 adds ReadSessionIdentity/ListSessions; canvas/v7 minor 1 adds UnselectWorldConnection, RetireSessionSelection, ListWorldSelections, ReserveWorldRetirement, ReleaseWorldRetirement. Existing operations keep their order and every existing type, field, enum value, ownership row and digest domain is unchanged; no new wire. The exact-package handshake still requires every composition to re-pin one package.

configEngineFacts.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; Adapter provider and Canvas consumer implementations and real runtime NOT_RUN
configEngineFacts.port: In-process method readConfigEngineFacts(worldRef) of the world source facts service (ConfigEngineFactsPort). Not a wire operation, model argument, tool or persisted record.
configEngineFacts.producer: world-source. writeBackend comes from the declaration of the world source payload actually loaded on the paired connection; avatarEnvelope is always the fixed UNAVAILABLE record below. No other origin produces, defaults or overrides either.
configEngineFacts.consumer: hanaworlds-canvas assembles CompilationConfig.writeBackend only from a validated KNOWN writeBackend (requireKnownWriteBackend), unchanged. No consumer assembles player geometry: SafetyProfile (safety-profile/v5) has no avatar size and comes only from safetyProfileFromConfirmedIntent; requireKnownAvatarEnvelope always refuses for anyone who asks for player geometry. Nothing persists player geometry. Brush, Painter, Workshop and Host consume only the assembled configuration.
configEngineFacts.writeBackend: writeBackend {profileId, revision} is the opaque identity of the write backend that the loaded world source payload uses to execute world-adapter/v8 scoped Prepare/Apply of compiled operations, as declared by that payload. adapterId, payloadVersion, capabilityRevision, a package or contracts version, or a default are not substitutes. NOT_DECLARED_BY_PAYLOAD when the loaded payload declares none; ENGINE_FACT_UNREADABLE when the declaration cannot be read.
configEngineFacts.domainAndLifecycle: Valid only for the exact connection {worldRef, connectionRef, connectionIncarnationRef} and catalogueDigest. The producer reads the connection before and after reading the declaration and fails with CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH or STALE_REVISION instead of returning a mixed result. A payload change, reconnect (new incarnation), Catalogue change or world change yields a different sourceRevision or a rejected read. Players joining, leaving or changing posture never change the record. No push: consumers re-read before each assembly and treat a different sourceRevision, connection or Catalogue as invalidating every CompilationConfig assembled from the previous fact.

avatarDimensions.rule: No contracts type carries player geometry: SafetyProfile (safety-profile/v5), RegionInspection, BodyWitness and EntranceWitness have no avatar size and no body cells. Body safety is decided inside the engine: inspection rejects footprints overlapping any connected player's actual box, and Prepare/apply recheck every written cell (INV-BODY-RECHECK-AT-PREPARE). Entrance sizing uses the skill-proposed, player-confirmed SiteRules.entranceClearance, a building design value that is not a player measurement. Actual collision boxes, extents, positions, yaw and posture stay inside the world source payload (INV-POSE-STAYS-IN-ENGINE).

configEngineFacts.notDecidedHere: requireBodyClearance is the non-switchable body invariant (true). requireEntranceConnectivity, entranceClearance, hazardPolicy and optionalLightRule are not World or Host configuration: the active skill proposes them, the player confirms them in Controls.siteRules, and ConfirmedIntent.siteRules is their only source; every SafetyProfile used with a confirmed intent carries exactly those values. Contracts fix no value, option list or default for them.

safetyCapabilities.meaning: Checks SiteRules.optionalLightRule against final-state light. No light witness kind exists in this major, so no peer can advertise it yet; a stated rule stays expressible and is refused by this name, never ignored.

The region write path has no entrance check. A confirmed requireEntranceConnectivity=true is refused on painter-region/v3 by this name; use the per-cell path or a rule without an entrance requirement.

guards.BODY_CLEARANCE: No solid node is written into any connected player's actual collision box (G1 at RESTORE/REGION_RESTORE).
guards.CELL_PROTECTION: The game's protection is asked for every written cell (G2). The declared protectionPrincipal says for whom; ANONYMOUS is not acting-principal protection.
guards.PLAYER_ENCLOSURE: No connected player who could leave the write's neighbourhood before the write is sealed in by it (G3). The predicate is the engine owner's design; no design size substitutes for it.

restore.causeCode: <the code of the failure that made the restore necessary>

engineGuards.rule: A response or receipt whose error comes from a guard carries guardRefusal; its error must equal guardRefusalError(guardRefusal, options) for one allowed form. Pre-flight GUARD_UNAVAILABLE: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/validate, nothing written. Restore stages (RESTORE, REGION_RESTORE) have two forms: (1) transaction form, when the restore's cause is known: RESTORE_FAILED/restore/RESTORE_ERROR pending manual recovery (AFTER_MANUAL_RECOVERY, PARTIAL) with causeCode = the failure that made the restore necessary; (2) engine form, when the writer has no cause (a stateless WriteRegion RESTORE, or an Undo): SAFETY_INVARIANT_FAILED (violation) or CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE (GUARD_UNAVAILABLE) with phase restore, mutationState NONE (the refused write wrote nothing), causeCode null. The transaction owner (Canvas) turns an engine-form refusal during a rollback into the transaction form and keeps the causing failure in applyFailure {error, guardRefusal} (error.causeCode equals applyFailure.error.code); during an Undo it returns the engine-form refusal unchanged with applyFailure null. A RESTORE_FAILED receipt always uses the transaction form.
engineGuards.notDecidedHere: No acting-principal identity source exists; ACTING_PRINCIPAL coverage cannot be declared truthfully until one is defined (INV text unchanged, INV-POSE PRESENTED).
engineGuards.relay: A guard refusal reaches the skill on the public wire: Adapter responses (world-adapter/v8, world-adapter-region/v3) -> Canvas responses (canvas/v7 ApplyRecoverableCommit, Undo, Redo, RecoverPendingUndo, ReadPendingUndoResult, InspectPlacementRegion; canvas-region/v3 ApplyRegionCommit, UndoRegionCommit) -> Workshop responses (session/v5 AdvanceCurrentBuild, UndoCurrentBuild, RecoverPendingUndo). Each carries guardRefusal beside error under the same rule; a relay passes the refusal and its error unchanged. Canvas's own pre-flight refusal (requireEngineGuards before any write) is GUARD_UNAVAILABLE with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/validate on the canvas/v7 or canvas-region/v3 envelope.

confirmedPlacement.meaning: Placement shown to the player before confirmation, as data rather than prose. Created only from a real RegionInspection (createPlacementProposal) and model or player selection; carried in Controls.placement (BriefProjection, reference-brief digest) and ConfirmedIntent.placement (intent digest). Absent means no structured placement was confirmed (the 1.0 meaning, unchanged); there is no null form.

kinds.EXACT_CELLS: Write exactly these world cells: the final effect positions must equal the cell set.
kinds.ANCHORED_EXTENT: A general building confirmed at a located range: every effect lies inside the bounds, on the same source inspection (no re-basing); cells inside it are not individually confirmed.

chain: session/v5 AppendMultimodalTurn controls.placement (pending, shown to the player)
session/v5 AnswerClarification: only a new human message confirms; ConfirmedIntent.placement equals BriefProjection.controls.placement
painter/v6 ValidateBuildProposal: request.regionInspection is the source inspection; effects match the target
painter/v6 CreateBuildPlan: validateCreateBuildPlanRequest/Response (source inspection before the model, planned operations after)
painter-region/v3 ValidateRegionProposal: specified world cells match the target

canvas-region/v3 ApplyRegionCommit confirmedPlacement: validateRegionCommitRequest checks it against the request operations; Canvas runs checkConfirmedRegionPlacementCommit with its own recorded inspection and current world revision before any snapshot or Adapter WriteRegion; validateRegionCommitSubmission makes Workshop send exactly the confirmed binding
canvas/v7 ApplyRecoverableCommit regionInspectionBinding.confirmedPlacement: Canvas rechecks its recorded inspection, current world revision and final effects before any write
validateCurrentBuildSubmission: the apply binding carries exactly the confirmed placement and intent digest

namedFailures.cases: effects are not the confirmed cells, or leave the confirmed extent
brief and confirmed intent placements differ; apply binding missing, invented or not the confirmed one; placement or intent digest does not match
the build or apply uses another inspection (for example a new CURRENT_VIEW) than the one the placement was proposed from
the world revision moved after the placement was proposed
the coordinate frame differs from the one the placement was proposed in
the request World is not the placement World
a proposed target is not inside the sampled bounds of its source inspection

confirmedPlacement.remedy: Every named failure is retryability AFTER_NEW_FACTS: make a new PlacementProposal from a current inspection and obtain a new human confirmation. Nothing is written.
confirmedPlacement.notDecidedHere: Which cells or range to propose, how it is displayed, and whether a building needs a structured placement at all are skill/Workshop decisions. Known-empty, body and engine guards are unchanged and still apply.

regionRollbackCause.meaning: The failure that made Canvas restore the whole region in a successful rollback (status ROLLED_BACK, actual summary equal to the before summary). The envelope keeps result XOR error, so a successful rollback has error null and applyFailure null; the cause therefore travels inside the result. A failed restore keeps the existing form (error RESTORE_FAILED with applyFailure) and has no result.
rules: Present only when status is ROLLED_BACK; a VERIFIED result carrying it is SCHEMA_INVALID/INVALID_SHAPE.
rollbackCause.error.phase is not restore (it is the failure that made the restore necessary).
rollbackCause.error.mutationState is NONE, PARTIAL or UNKNOWN: the world state at the failing step, before the restore.
rollbackCause.error.transactionRef is null or the result transactionId: the cause lives inside this transaction's result and never names another transaction.
rollbackCause.guardRefusal, when not null, explains rollbackCause.error exactly (guardRefusalError); an Adapter WriteRegion error and guard refusal that caused the restore are relayed unchanged.
Absent means the cause is not reported: consumers read it as UNKNOWN (regionRollbackCauseOf returns cause UNKNOWN), never as a default or guessed cause. It is the 1.1 meaning, unchanged.
regionRollbackCause.readRoute: The ApplyRegionCommit response of that request. Canvas stores the terminal response (including rollbackCause) with the request outcome; an exact replay of the same request (validateCurrentRequest disposition RETURN_STORED) returns it unchanged and never writes again. No QueryTransaction exists for regions; per-cell QueryTransaction and Adapter last-call facts are not this route.
notCovered: Cells outside the transaction's operation boxes and natural simulation or other writers: neither restored nor attributed.
Test or bridge instrumentation identity: the cause reports what Canvas observed, not who injected it.

worldSourceFacts.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE normative definition; world source (adapter), host bridge and Canvas implementations and real runtime NOT_RUN
worldSourceFacts.meaning: Named operations through which the world source declares its facts (C-world-facts, C-world-adapter ReadWorldSourceCapabilities) and the host bridge gives the current inspection context (C-world-inspection). They replace the engine-shaped in-process facts ports (Catalogue reads, config-engine-facts/v2) for new consumers; those ports and types stay unchanged in this major.
worldSourceFacts.domainAndLifecycle: Every world source fact is valid only for the exact connection {worldRef, connectionRef, connectionIncarnationRef} it names and, where it carries one, the catalogueDigest of the Catalogue it was read with. Consumers re-read before each use and reject a fact of another connection (CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH) or another Catalogue (CATALOGUE_MISMATCH). No push.
worldSourceFacts.unavailable: A fact the world source cannot give is a named UNAVAILABLE or null-as-unknown value, never a default. requireWriteProfileConfig and requireDeclaredAvatarEnvelope refuse with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/validate/REQUIRED_FACT_UNKNOWN.
worldSourceFacts.forwarding: The host bridge forwards WriteProfile unchanged: it does not interpret, complete or default compilationConfig, writeMethods or avatarEnvelope.
worldSourceFacts.avatarEnvelope: The body envelope is a size the world source declares (D-17, WORLD-ABSTRACTION.md section 0.1 B6), not a measurement of a connected player: no position, yaw, posture or identity is representable (KnownAvatarEnvelope has only availability, basis and size). config-engine-facts/v2 is unchanged and keeps its fixed UNAVAILABLE record; SafetyProfile still carries no body size.
worldSourceFacts.writePath: hasSideEffects/hasPersistentState are conclusions the world source derives from its own engine (C6). A Catalogue material whose placeable tag is true must have path and material conclusions both false; placeable false or null is always allowed.
worldSourceFacts.errors: The errors listed per operation are the operation errors of that call; decoding (SCHEMA_INVALID, UNKNOWN_REQUIRED_FIELD, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION) and currency (CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH, CATALOGUE_MISMATCH) refusals apply to every call.

brushPlacementMinor.blockDigest: Optional blockDigest is digestValue('region-block', chunk.block).sha256 over the SDK canonical RegionVoxelBlock. CompileRegionBuild providers return it for every chunk; SDK verifies it whenever present. Absence preserves old 2.0.0 input and digest meaning.
brushPlacementMinor.geometryProfile: Optional open geometry profile reference on the shared footprint used by canvas/v7 InspectPlacementRegion and world-adapter/v8 InspectRegion. Old inputs decode unchanged. Neutral Canvas admission requires it explicitly and checks the current ReadLocalConnection worldGeometry declaration. Missing: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/REQUIRED_FACT_UNKNOWN; unsupported: CAPABILITY_GAP/GEOMETRY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED. Dimensions remain integer grid dimensions; this minor defines no non-voxel success shape. Never add the field to an older closed Adapter wire.
brushPlacementMinor.evidence: SOURCE/FIXTURE only; Brush and Canvas provider implementation belongs to brush-01 and canvas-01.

rules: creationFacts and engineProfile are strict JSON owned by the world source. Carry unchanged; hosts never interpret them.
Template IDs, labels, prerequisites and delete impacts are declared by the provider; no engine template is prescribed.
Every response binds requestId and shared world, template, display name, confirmation and connection selectors.
Delete requires the current provider confirmationName and bridge verification of no live session selection. JSON alone cannot prove this.
launch/start/pair receipts refer to actual connection incarnations; providers must read back the real connection.
play ENTERED is only returned after the graphical client actually entered the selected world; canPlay absence is a refusal.
UNKNOWN runtime status asserts no running or stopped fact. STOPPED and ENTERED are provider observations, never inferred from timers.
Contracts validate pure data only; fixture mocks have no process, filesystem, connection or world side effects.

describeSourceWorld is a read-only optional LocalWorldsPort capability. Success binds exactly to the requested worldRef, never displayName; missing worlds return WORLD_NOT_FOUND, unavailable source returns ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE, identity or reference inconsistencies return CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH. A consumer with no method explicitly reports CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE.

sourceLocator is strict opaque JSON describing the locator at read time. Only the paired adapter/local-runtime world source interprets it. It grants no startup, write or delete authority, supplies no persistent identity or freshness proof, and must not enter any C-world-lifecycle host field. creationFacts retains its original meaning and shape.

sourceStartupFacts is optional strict opaque JSON supplied by the paired world source from its current verified payload. Only that source interprets it; callers cannot self-report engine permissions, and missing/stale observations never imply startup authority.

toolManifest.boundary: Model arguments are input only. The host injects hostContext and image-material catalogueFacts from the current session and paired world. Providers must admit against independently read host/source facts; model arguments cannot select a session/world or assert confirmation.

directBuild.scope: Exact canonical proposalDigest plus the host-authorized ConfirmedIntent. The host independently establishes that the proposal fits the actual current user request and allowed intent scope; unknown or changed scope has no authorization.
directBuild.digest: Lowercase SHA-256 of RFC 8785 canonical JSON, UTF-8, of the entire CurrentBuildUserRequest (messageDigest) or neutral DirectBuildProposal (proposalDigest). No existing projection/domain changes.
directBuild.consumption: validateToolRequest with independently read currentUserRequest and stored intentAuthorization before every execution or replay. The request carrier must equal stored authorization. Re-read current message/session/turn revision/world before committing; no old-message reuse. Structural admission alone does not authorize.
pipeline: fresh world-source facts and placement inspection
non-disableable safety invariants and engine guards
directBuild.otherObjects: OTHER_OBJECTS_AFFECTED always refuses; original continue confirmation is required.

buildingSkill.name: hanaworlds-building
buildingSkill.description: Consume the current turn text and image attachment references. Return a clarification, a pending proposal, or a declared plugin tool call. The host alone supplies current session, turn and world; the model cannot self-report them. Choose per-cell or region writes using current world-source declarations, never engine vocabulary in the skill. Confirmed proposal state belongs to Workshop; apply cannot accept a model confirmation. Image material matching belongs to Painter and uses source colours with CIEDE2000, zero model calls and zero world writes. Only the seven declared tools and their declared actions are permitted. For a clear current user request, emit hanaworlds_build action=build with a neutral BUILD or REGION proposal. The current request itself is the approved direct-build user input; no second confirmation reply is required. Only independently read and stored host authorization bound to this message, session, turn revision, world and exact allowed proposal/intent scope permits execution. Model clear/confirmed claims and valid shape are never authorization. Ambiguous requirements use pending proposal clarification and formal confirmation. Painter validation, fresh world facts, placement checks and mandatory safety invariants precede existing Brush/Canvas commits. OTHER_OBJECTS_AFFECTED always stops for the existing continue confirmation.

worldErrorContext.meaning: Optional. The target world this admitted operation actually needed. Not the currently available/selected world, not a file path, never derived from model input, raw JSON, another Session or an exception message.
worldErrorContext.absence: Absent keeps exactly the previous meaning: the error carries no world context. There is no null form; providers omit the field when no target can be determined.
worldErrorContext.binding: When the request carries a top-level worldRef selector, or a tool request carries host-injected hostContext.localContext.worldRef, a response error worldRef must equal it (CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH). Without a selector the provider sets it only from its own trusted current-Session/operation binding; consumers cannot verify that source and must not treat it as a selection.
worldErrorContext.unchanged: code, phase, retryability, mutationState, transactionRef, causeCode and reason keep their vocabulary and meaning. The world reference is never encoded into reason or transactionRef; no free message, path, credential or stack is added.
worldErrorContext.carrier: ContractError details.worldRef -> publicError.worldRef; omitted when not supplied. An invalid worldRef (not a non-empty string) is a programmer error (TypeError), never silently dropped.
worldErrorContext.compatibility: Same package major. Old errors without the field stay valid with unchanged digests. A previous-minor strict decoder (additionalProperties:false) refuses an error carrying worldRef with UNKNOWN_REQUIRED_FIELD; consuming it requires >= 2.7.0. No protocol minor requirement is added.

historicalReceipt.meaning: Optional pair. A durable receipt read back after a stop/reconnect keeps the localContext it was written with (connectionIncarnationRef, selectionRevision, connectionRef) and its receipt digest. The response envelope names the current context in currentLocalContext; result is the historical ReceiptProjection exactly as written, never re-bound to the current incarnation.
historicalReceipt.absence: Both absent keeps exactly the previous meaning: result.localContext must equal the request localContext in full. There is no null form; the two fields are present together or not at all, only beside a non-null result and a null error (otherwise SCHEMA_INVALID).
historicalReceipt.binding: currentLocalContext must equal the request localContext in full (CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH; currency is not relaxed). receiptDigest must equal the receipt digest of result (NON_CANONICAL_AMBIGUITY), the same value as HistoryEntry.receiptDigest. result.localContext.worldRef must equal the request worldRef (CURRENT_WORLD_MISMATCH). result.transactionId and result.transactionPayloadDigest must equal the request (TRANSACTION_CONFLICT); result.operationDigest is bound through receiptDigest. result.localContext.connectionRef, connectionIncarnationRef and selectionRevision may differ from the current context and are read with readHistoricalReceipt.
historicalReceipt.unchanged: Every other operation, and QueryTransaction responses without the pair, keep the full-equality localContext check. ReceiptProjection, its digest and every old fixture are unchanged. A receipt from another world is still refused.
historicalReceipt.compatibility: Same package major; world-adapter protocol minor 2 -> 3. A previous-minor strict decoder (additionalProperties:false) refuses a response carrying the pair with UNKNOWN_REQUIRED_FIELD; consuming it requires >= 2.8.0. A consumer that needs historical receipts requires world-adapter minor 3.

pluginRoles.meaning: Read-only: which running plugins currently fill each HanaWorlds role. The provider derives it from what the host actually registered, through this published evidence table only.

identity.service: A service evidence names a Cordis service. Its provider is the plugin that registered it in the running host: the loader module specifier (moduleName) of the nearest fiber, from the providing fiber upward, that carries a loader entry. Only services whose providing fiber is active count.
identity.skill: A skill evidence names a skill in the host skill registry (ctx.skills). Its provider is the SkillSummary.provider of every live catalog entry with that name. The DSH skill registry does not expose the registering plugin, so this identity is the registered skill provider name, not a loader module specifier.

pluginRoles.status: COMPLETE when missingRoles is empty; UNAVAILABLE when every required role is missing; PARTIAL otherwise.
pluginRoles.failure: A read that cannot be completed (service store unreadable, a providing fiber with no loader entry, a skill catalog that is incomplete or throws) is the response error CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/validate/REQUIRED_FACT_UNKNOWN with result null. It is never answered as empty providers or as a status.
pluginRoles.forbidden: Never inferred from package names, bundle names, hand-written configuration or seeds. No versions.
pluginRoles.compatibility: Same package major; world-inspection protocol minor 0 -> 1. New operation and new types only; every old type, operation and digest is unchanged. A consumer that needs ReadPluginRoles requires world-inspection minor 1.

placementSettingsRead.currentValues: Only the bound world placementSettings, synchronized to the currently effective Canvas Config; descriptor defaults are display/documentation metadata, never current-value evidence. Missing/invalid/unsynchronized policy: CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE/validate/POLICY_UNAVAILABLE, no repair or hidden defaults.
placementSettingsRead.scope: Identity verified through the existing session port before and after the read; session revision, active world, full localContext, saved/live connection and settingsRevision must remain current. Null localContext only permits requesting an unbound error; never a successful read. No replay cache.

surface.placementSettingDescriptors: Existing export supplies name/owner/default/scope/meaning/consequence; show result.placementSettings as current. Config is plugin-wide and synchronized to bound worlds only by existing startup/selection behavior; save and reload to take effect.
surface.placementInvariants: Existing export; switchable=false, show read-only. Search distance zero never disables engine guards, body checks or recoverable transactions.
surface.SafetyProfile: Existing SafetyProfile and safetyProfileFromConfirmedIntent; only confirmed intent supplies site rules. No body size, no Canvas setting/default provider; this read does not construct or modify it.
surface.AvatarEnvelope: Existing AvatarEnvelope: world source declared body size, not connected-player measurements. Supplied via existing WriteProfile/WorldSourceCapabilities; unknown remains UNAVAILABLE. Canvas does not read or fabricate it here; other provider semantics are unchanged.
